learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the step-by-step blueprint used by data scientists to build an AI project, from defining the problem to testing the final model!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: This is the first stage where you define the goal of your AI project. We use the '4Ws Canvas' to frame the problem: Who (is facing it?), What (is the problem?), Where (does it happen?), and Why (is it worth solving?).
AI needs data to learn! This stage involves collecting accurate and reliable data related to your problem from various sources like sensors, cameras, surveys, or government databases.
Raw data is often messy. Data Exploration involves cleaning the data and creating visual graphs (like bar charts or scatter plots) to spot trends, patterns, and anomalies before training the AI.

Modelling is where the AI actually learns. We can use a 'Rule-based' approach (developer writes the rules) or a 'Learning-based' approach (machine discovers rules from data). Finally, Evaluation tests the model's accuracy on new data.

fun_activity.title: 📝 The 4Ws of School Traffic
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you want to build an AI to solve the traffic jam outside your school at 2 PM. Fill out the 4Ws Canvas: WHO are the stakeholders? WHAT is the exact issue? WHERE does it happen? WHY does it need to be solved?

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the 5 stages of the AI Project Cycle in order: Problem Scoping -> Data Acquisition -> Data Exploration -> Modelling -> Evaluation.
📌 The 4Ws are Who, What, Where, and Why. Be ready to apply them to a hypothetical scenario given in the exam.
📌 Rule-based models follow static 'If-Then' rules written by humans. Learning-based models dynamically figure out the patterns themselves using Machine Learning.
quick_recap: ⭐ An AI project always starts with clearly scoping the problem using the 4Ws.
⭐ Data must be acquired, cleaned, and explored visually before feeding it to an algorithm.
⭐ Models are evaluated using testing data to ensure they perform well in the real world.
